newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's to host professional indemnity conference.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's to host professional indemnity conference.

text.p: Lloyd's of London is to hold its first professional indemnity conference next week, in what it hopes may become an annual event.

The two day conference at Alexandra Palace in North London is the first of its type organised by Lloyd's and will cover future trends in professional indemnity insurance and global issues affecting the industry.
The move marks an effort to emphasise to clients the cohesive nature of Lloyd's, underlining what it sees as its unique strengths and competitive edge.

"Professional indemnity, including directors' and officers' insurance, accounts for 10 percent of Lloyd's global premium income. Our position in the market means that there is a tremendous wealth of knowledge and expertise to be pooled," said Lloyd's chairman Sir David Rowland.
The 300 year-old insurance market is increasingly aware of the need to respond to the competitive pressures it faces around the world.

The unwanted publicity generated by the huge losses of the 1980s and early 1990s which nearly destroyed it and the subsequent very public court cases involving some Names - its traditional backers - suing underwriters for negligence, has been difficult for Lloyd's to shake-off.
It has already taken a number of steps designed to improve its image but the events of the last couple of years has had a profound, and damaging effect on Lloyd's reputation particularly in the U.S.
At the beginning of the year Lloyd's reorganised its internal structure in an effort to improve customer service.
That theme was underlined only last week at its annual meeting where Sir David Rowland stressed the need to respond to customer needs, competition and the changing market.

Less than a month ago the Council of Lloyd's endorsed a working party report calling for the introduction of external regulation of the market for the first time in the hope of boosting confidence in the market.
Some 350 delegates are expected to attend next week's conference including many North American clients as well as Lloyd's underwriters and brokers.
The main topics to be discussed at the conference include the future of Lloyd's, insurance trends, the impact of the computer "millennium timebomb" and the effects on business of globalisation.
